name: Tirzepatide

lead: Tirzepatide is a once-weekly injectable from Eli Lilly that activates both the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 receptors. It is sold as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and as Zepbound for chronic weight management, and in phase 3 trials it produced the largest average weight reductions of any approved anti-obesity drug.

For looksmaxxing it serves as a systemic fat-loss tool. As with other incretin drugs, facial leaning follows total fat loss rather than being targeted, and because the weight loss is larger, facial volume loss and skin laxity can be more noticeable in some users.

paras: Tirzepatide is a modified peptide that acts as an agonist at the GIP and GLP-1 receptors, with stronger activity at GIP. GLP-1 signalling reduces appetite, slows gastric emptying and supports insulin secretion; GIP signalling is thought to add to appetite suppression and may improve tolerability and adipose tissue handling. The combined effect lowers calorie intake and improves glycaemic control.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are common, mostly during dose escalation. Pancreatitis, gallbladder disease and dehydration-related kidney injury have been reported, and the label carries a thyroid C-cell tumour warning. It can reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives. Lean mass loss accompanies fat loss, and weight returns after discontinuation. It is prescription-only; unregulated peptide-vial sources add contamination and dosing-accuracy risks.
